close_reason: fixed: now_utc_string includes sub-second (millisecond) precision via subsec_millis(); pre-epoch case handled by negating the duration rather than returning 0
description: crate-jmap-server/src/helpers.rs now_utc_string() uses a hand-rolled Gregorian calendar algorithm (Howard Hinnant) and returns seconds-resolution RFC 3339. RFC 8621 §4.1.6 specifies UTCDate as an RFC 3339 string with at least second precision. While the format is valid, (1) any platform where SystemTime::now() predates UNIX_EPOCH (container drift) silently returns 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, as noted in the comment; (2) two emails created within the same second will have identical receivedAt, which breaks stable sort ordering in tests and can confuse thread ordering. This is particularly risky because sort-by-receivedAt is a comparator the test backend depends on for correctness.
title: now_utc_string uses hand-rolled date algorithm; no sub-second precision for receivedAt
